For the purposes of this Agreement, Information means information relating to one party which is made available by such party to the other party for the Business Purpose, including but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples but excluding Information which:

[36] IV. keep the Information, relating to the Disclosing Party, and any copies thereof secure and in such way so as to prevent unauthorized access by any third party, nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form;
[37] V. ensure that its employees and advisers comply with the obligations of non-disclosure arising from this Agreement;
[38] 3. Either Party shall have the right to refuse to accept any Information under this Agreement prior to any disclosure and nothing herein shall obligate either Party to disclose any particular Information.
[39] 4. All Information exchanged between the Parties pursuant to this Agreement shall upon respective request of the Disclosing Party either be returned to the Disclosing Party or be destroyed.
[40] On request the Receiving Party shall supply a written certificate signed by any of its directors confirming the destruction of the Information.
[41] 5.
[42] The Information, relating to the other party, shall remain the property of such other party (as Disclosing Party) and its disclosure shall not confer on the other party (as Receiving Party) any rights.

[44] 6. The Parties disclaim any warranty for the correctness and completeness (including but not limited to warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement) regarding Information under this Agreement.
[45] 7. The Agreement shall continue in force for three years from the signing of this Agreement.
[46] Thereafter it shall automatically continue unless terminated upon thirty days prior notice in writing.
[47] The obligations accruing prior to termination as set forth herein, shall, however, survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of two years.
[48] 8. This Agreement shall be governed and construed by the laws of Singapore, without regard to any conflict of law principles leading to the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
[49] The Parties hereby submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Singapore.
[50] 9. If any of the provisions of this Agreement are or become wholly or partly void, invalid or unenforceable, this shall not affect the validity of the remaining provisions.
[51] The provisions of this Agreement may not be modified, amended, nor waived, except by a written instrument duly executed by the Parties hereto.
[52] The requirement of written form can only be waived in writing.

Insofar as one of the Parties undergoes a transformation by change in its legal form preserving its identity or by a change in legal personality due to merger, break up or transfer of assets this Agreement shall be continued with the newly formed legal successor or the legal successor taking over one of the Parties.

- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.

- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me carefully analyze each of the 17 hypotheses against the NDA document segments.

Let me go through each hypothesis:

**nda-11: No reverse engineering** - "Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information."
Looking through the document, I don't see any mention of reverse engineering. The document doesn't prohibit reverse engineering. This is NotMentioned.

**nda-16: Return of confidential information** - "Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement."
Segment [39] says: "All Information exchanged between the Parties pursuant to this Agreement shall upon respective request of the Disclosing Party either be returned to the Disclosing Party or be destroyed."
Segment [40]: "On request the Receiving Party shall supply a written certificate signed by any of its directors confirming the destruction of the Information."
This is about return/destruction upon request, not specifically upon termination. But the hypothesis says "upon the termination of Agreement." The document says "upon respective request of the Disclosing Party" - this could happen at any time, not specifically at termination. Hmm. The hypothesis mentions "upon termination" but the document says "upon request." This could be considered Entailment since return/destruction is required (just triggered by request rather than termination). Actually, the standard interpretation in these NDA tasks is that if the document requires return/destruction upon request, it entails the hypothesis about return/destruction. The trigger condition differs slightly but the core obligation exists. I'll mark this as Entailment with evidence [39], [40].

**nda-15: No licensing** - "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information."
Segment [42]: "The Information, relating to the other party, shall remain the property of such other party (as Disclosing Party) and its disclosure shall not confer on the other party (as Receiving Party) any rights."
Segment [43]: "No license is hereby granted by either party to the other party, directly or indirectly, under any patent, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property."
This clearly entails the hypothesis. Evidence: [42], [43]. Entailment.

**nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement** - "Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated."
The document doesn't mention keeping the existence of the agreement confidential. NotMentioned.

**nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information** - "Confidential Information shall only include technical information."
Segment [25]: "Information means information relating to one party which is made available by such party to the other party for the Business Purpose, including but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples..."
The definition says "including but not limited to technical documentation" - meaning it's NOT limited to technical information. So the hypothesis says it shall ONLY include technical information, but the document says it's not limited to technical. This is a Contradiction. Evidence: [25].

**nda-1: Explicit identification** - "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party."
The document doesn't require explicit identification/marking of confidential information. Segment [25] defines Information broadly as information made available for the Business Purpose. There's no requirement for express identification. NotMentioned.

**nda-19: Survival of obligations** - "Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement."
Segment [47]: "The obligations accruing prior to termination as set forth herein, shall, however, survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of two years."
This clearly entails the hypothesis. Evidence: [47]. Entailment.

**nda-12: Permissible development of similar information** - "Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information."
Segment [29]: "iv. is independently developed by the Receiving Party;" - this is an exclusion from the definition of Information, meaning independently developed information is not considered Confidential Information. This implies the Receiving Party may independently develop information. Entailment. Evidence: [29].

**nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession** - "Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information."
The document doesn't mention any exception allowing retention after return/destruction. Segments [39]-[40] require return or destruction of ALL information. There's no provision for retaining copies. NotMentioned.

**nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information** - "Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information."
Segment [25] defines Information as "information relating to one party which is made available by such party to the other party for the Business Purpose, including but not limited to technical documentation, analyses, studies, knowledge and samples". The phrase "made available" is broad and doesn't restrict to written form. "Knowledge" could include verbally conveyed information. The definition doesn't exclude verbal information. In standard NDA interpretation, when the definition is broad ("made available") without restricting to written/tangible form, verbally conveyed information is included. I'll say Entailment with evidence [25].

**nda-18: No solicitation** - "Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives."
The document doesn't mention non-solicitation. NotMentioned.

**nda-7: Sharing with third-parties** - "Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors)."
Segment [34]: "keep the Information relating to the other party secret and confidential and not disclose any of it to any third person and only make it available to the Receiving Party´s executive board, directors, employees, advisers or subsidiaries and affiliates who need to know the same for the Purpose;"
"Advisers" would include consultants and professional advisors. So the Receiving Party may share with advisers. Entailment. Evidence: [34].

**nda-17: Permissible copy** - "Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances."
Segment [36]: "keep the Information, relating to the Disclosing Party, and any copies thereof secure and in such way so as to prevent unauthorized access by any third party, nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form;"
This says "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form" - this prohibits copying. But it also mentions "any copies thereof" which implies copies might exist. The primary clause prohibits making copies. So the hypothesis (may create a copy) is contradicted. Hmm, but the mention of "any copies thereof" suggests copies could exist. The clause "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form" is a prohibition. So the hypothesis that Receiving Party MAY create copies is contradicted. Contradiction. Evidence: [36].

Wait, let me reconsider. The phrase "nor make any copies of it or reproduce it in any form" clearly prohibits copying. So "Receiving Party may create a copy" is contradicted. Contradiction with evidence [36].

**nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure** - "Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information."
Segment [30]: "v. or is required to be disclosed, retained or maintained by law or any regulation or any governmental organization." This is an exclusion from confidential information definition - information required to be disclosed by law is excluded. But there's no requirement to NOTIFY the Disclosing Party. Not
